clinician.trajectory_summary: A 27-year-old woman with no underlying medical conditions presented with a 2-day history of bilateral, progressively oedematous and pruritic toes. Initial examination revealed multiple bilateral non-haemorrhagic bullae up to 1.5 cm in diameter on the dorsa of the toes with widespread erythema, oedema, and pain when confined by shoes. No acrocyanosis or livedo reticularis was present. Two days following initial presentation, the bullae progressed to become haemorrhagic, with no other clinical changes, petechiae, or signs of bruising or bleeding elsewhere. Notably, the patient had experienced 10 days of ageusia and anosmia 6 weeks prior to the toe manifestation, consistent with prior COVID-19 infection. Subsequent SARS-CoV-2 testing was positive, confirming COVID-19 association with the dermatologic manifestation. At 3-month follow-up, the acral oedema and pruritus had completely resolved, and the bullous lesions healed with residual scaling and cutaneous violaceous hyperpigmentation. The patient remained otherwise asymptomatic at follow-up.
